A [Singapore passport](/wiki/Singaporean_passport "Singaporean passport") from 2018

**Visa requirements for Singapore citizens** are administrative entry restrictions by the authorities of other states which are imposed on citizens of the [Republic of Singapore](/wiki/Republic_of_Singapore "Republic of Singapore").

As of 2026, holders of [Singapore passports](/wiki/Singapore_passport "Singapore passport") have visa-free/visa-on-arrival/ electronic visa access to a total of 192 countries and territories, ranking the Singapore passport 1st in the world according to [Henley Passport Index](/wiki/Henley_Passport_Index "Henley Passport Index").[[1]](#cite_note-1)

Instruments associated with classical music, including the violin and piano, were invented in Italy.[[368]](#cite_note-Erlich-374)

From [folk](/wiki/Italian_folk_music "Italian folk music") to [classical](/wiki/European_classical_music "European classical music"), music is an intrinsic part of Italian culture. Instruments associated with classical music, including the piano and violin, were invented in Italy,[[368]](#cite_note-Erlich-374) and many prevailing forms, such as the [symphony](/wiki/Symphony "Symphony"), concerto, and [sonata](/wiki/Sonata "Sonata"), trace their roots back to innovations in 16th- and 17th-century Italian music.

Italy's most famous composers include the Renaissance [Palestrina](/wiki/Giovanni_Pierluigi_da_Palestrina "Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina"), [Monteverdi](/wiki/Monteverdi "Monteverdi"), and [Gesualdo](/wiki/Carlo_Gesualdo "Carlo Gesualdo"); the [Baroque](/wiki/Baroque_music "Baroque music") [Scarlatti](/wiki/Domenico_Scarlatti "Domenico Scarlatti"), and [Vivaldi](/wiki/Vivaldi "Vivaldi"); the classical [Paganini](/wiki/Paganini "Paganini"), and [Rossini](/wiki/Rossini "Rossini"); and the Romantic [Verdi](/wiki/Verdi "Verdi") and [Puccini](/wiki/Puccini "Puccini"). Classical music has a strong hold in Italy, as evidenced by the fame of its opera houses, such as La Scala, and performers such as the pianist [Maurizio Pollini](/wiki/Maurizio_Pollini "Maurizio Pollini") and tenor [Luciano Pavarotti](/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti "Luciano Pavarotti"). Main articles: [Dodgers–Yankees rivalry](/wiki/Dodgers%E2%80%93Yankees_rivalry "Dodgers–Yankees rivalry") and [Subway Series](/wiki/Subway_Series "Subway Series")

The Dodgers and the Yankees have met 12 times in the [World Series](/wiki/World_Series "World Series"), more than any other two teams from the [American](/wiki/American_League "American League") and [National Leagues](/wiki/National_League_(baseball) "National League (baseball)").[[85]](#cite_note-YankeesDodgers-86) The rivalry began when the Dodgers played in [Brooklyn](/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn"), and the two teams faced each other in seven [Subway Series](/wiki/Subway_Series "Subway Series") in the 1940s and 1950s.

After the Dodgers moved to Los Angeles in [1958](/wiki/1958_in_baseball "1958 in baseball"), the rivalry continued as the teams represented two of the largest cities on each coast of the United States. Fan support has added to the notoriety of the series as both teams are supported by two of the largest fanbases in North America.[[86]](#cite_note-87)

Although the rivalry's significance arose from the two teams' numerous World Series meetings, the Yankees and Dodgers did not meet in the World Series between [1981](/wiki/1981_World_Series "1981 World Series") and [2024](/wiki/2024_World_Series "2024 World Series").[[85]](#cite_note-YankeesDodgers-86) They did not play each other again in a non-exhibition game until 2004, when they played a three-game [interleague](/wiki/Interleague_play "Interleague play") series.[[87]](#cite_note-88) Nevertheless, games between the two teams have drawn sellout crowds.[[88]](#cite_note-Sellouts-89)

The rivalry between the Dodgers and the [Houston Astros](/wiki/Houston_Astros "Houston Astros") began as a divisional matchup, but hostility waned after Houston moved to the American League. In 2017, the two teams faced off in the [2017 World Series](/wiki/2017_World_Series "2017

In October 2022, OPEC+ led by Saudi Arabia announced a large cut to its oil output target in order to aid Russia.[[175]](#cite_note-175)[[176]](#cite_note-176) In response, US President [Joe Biden](/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") vowed "consequences" and said the US government would "re-evaluate" the longstanding [U.S. relationship with Saudi Arabia](/wiki/Saudi_Arabia%E2%80%93United_States_relations "Saudi Arabia–United States relations").[[177]](#cite_note-177) [Robert Menendez](/wiki/Robert_Menendez "Robert Menendez"), the Democratic chairman of the U.S. Senate Foreign Relations Committee, called for a freeze on cooperation with and arms sales to Saudi Arabia, accusing the kingdom of helping Russia underwrite its war with Ukraine.[[178]](#cite_note-178)

Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry stated that the OPEC+ decision was "purely economic" and taken unanimously by all members of the conglomerate, pushing back on pressure to change its stance on the Russo-Ukrainian War at the UN.[[179]](#cite_note-179)[[180]](#cite_note-180) In response, the White House accused Saudi Arabia of pressuring other OPEC nations into agreeing with the production cut, some of which felt coerced, saying the United States had presented the Saudi government with an analysis showing there was no market basis for the cut. The Sahara covers large parts of [Algeria](/wiki/Algeria "Algeria"), [Chad](/wiki/Chad "Chad"), [Egypt](/wiki/Egypt "Egypt"), [Libya](/wiki/Libya "Libya"), [Mali](/wiki/Mali "Mali"), [Mauritania](/wiki/Mauritania "Mauritania"), [Niger](/wiki/Niger "Niger"), [Western Sahara](/wiki/Western_Sahara "Western Sahara") and [Sudan](/wiki/Sudan "Sudan"), and parts of southern [Morocco](/wiki/Morocco "Morocco") and [Tunisia](/wiki/Tunisia "Tunisia"). It covers 9 million square kilometres (3,500,000 sq mi), 31% of the African continent. If all areas with a mean annual precipitation of less than 250 mm (9.8 in) were included, the Sahara would be 11 million square kilometres (4,200,000 sq mi). It is one of three distinct [physiographic provinces](/wiki/Physiographic_provinces "Physiographic provinces") of the [African massive physiographic division](/wiki/Physiographic_regions_of_the_world#Compendium_table_of_the_worlds_physiographic_regions "Physiographic regions of the world"). The Sahara is so large and bright that, in theory, it could be detected from other stars as a surface feature of Earth, with near-current technology.[[10]](#cite_note-10)

Kéré at the 2024 World Economic Forum

Kéré was one of three architects chosen to design a permanent exhibition space at the [International Red Cross and Red Crescent Museum](/wiki/International_Red_Cross_and_Red_Crescent_Museum "International Red Cross and Red Crescent Museum"), which opened in 2012 in Geneva, Switzerland. Each architect worked on a theme; Gringo Cardia (from Brazil) focused on “defending human dignity”, [Shigeru Ban](/wiki/Shigeru_Ban "Shigeru Ban") (from Japan) focused on “refusing fatality” and Kéré selected the theme “reconstructing the family link”.

Kéré contributed the dark entrance passage, bounded by hemp concrete walls, that encourages the visitor to consider the frightened and suffocating emotions of family tragedy during conflict. Central to this part of the exhibition is a tower, also made of hemp concrete, which is an architectural reference to a traditional hut for a nuclear family. It lets in very little light and has a [Corten steel](/wiki/Corten_Steel "Corten Steel") floor with a rusty appearance. This space is a memorial to tragedies such as the [Srebrenica massacre](/wiki/Srebrenica_massacre "Srebrenica massacre"). A Tree of Messages, with metal branches, was built to serve as a reminder of the cold contrast between nature and war. fanoutqa_035818.x:
Major League Baseball :: History :: The modern game :: chunk_0014
In recent years, with the advent of technologies such as [Statcast](/wiki/Statcast "Statcast") and its use of [Hawk-Eye](/wiki/Hawk-Eye "Hawk-Eye") starting in 2020[[91]](#cite_note-92) as well as with advanced statistics as provided by sites such as [FanGraphs](/wiki/FanGraphs "FanGraphs") and Baseball Savant, MLB has evolved. With the ability to see precise movements of pitchers and batters, teams can assess the mechanics of a player and help them improve. Statcast also provides some features such as tracking the paths of most batted balls, tracking the speed of most batted balls, and tracking the [exit velocity](/wiki/Exit_velocity "Exit velocity") of most batted balls. Statcast has allowed for advanced defensive analytics that have not been possible before tracking of players due to how subjective fielding can be.

The rate of teams using a [defensive shift](/wiki/Defensive_shift "Defensive shift") went up from 13.7% in 2016 to 33.6% in 2022 because advanced statistics supported this as an effective way to stop hitters from getting hits.[[92]](#cite_note-93) Because the shift reduces the number of balls in play that result in hits and MLB wishes to increase interest in baseball, MLB announced in September 2022 that extreme infield defensive shifts would be banned starting in 2023. To be compliant, there must be two fielders on each side of second base, and those fielders must have both of their feet on the infield dirt at the time the pitch is thrown. If this rule is not followed, the choice of an automatic ball or the outcome of the play is given to the batting team.[[93]](#cite_note-:0-94)

The game of baseball has also slowed down significantly due to an increased number of strikeouts and walks—two outcomes that generally take many pitches to complete—and an increased amount of time taken for a pitcher to pitch. In 1997, President [Bill Clinton](/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") nominated her to the [U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit](/wiki/U.S._Court_of_Appeals_for_the_Second_Circuit "U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit"). That appointment was slowed by the [Republican](/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") majority in the [United States Senate](/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") because of its concerns that the position might lead to a Supreme Court nomination, but she was confirmed in 1998. On the Second Circuit, Sotomayor heard appeals in more than 3,000 cases and wrote about 380 opinions. Sotomayor has taught at the [New York University School of Law](/wiki/New_York_University_School_of_Law "New York University School of Law") and [Columbia Law School](/wiki/Columbia_Law_School "Columbia Law School").

In May 2009, President Obama nominated Sotomayor to the Supreme Court following Justice [David Souter](/wiki/David_Souter "David Souter")'s retirement. Her nomination was confirmed by the Senate in August 2009 by a vote of 68–31. While on the Court, Sotomayor has supported the informal liberal bloc of justices when they divide along the commonly perceived ideological lines. During her Supreme Court tenure, Sotomayor has been identified with concern for the rights of criminal defendants and criminal justice reform, as demonstrated in majority opinions such as *[J. D. [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/Persian_Cat_01.jpg/250px-Persian_Cat_01.jpg)](/wiki/File:Persian_Cat_01.jpg)

Cream adult as a pet in an Iranian house

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Chocolate_Persian.jpg/250px-Chocolate_Persian.jpg)](/wiki/File:Chocolate_Persian.jpg)

A [Grand Champion](/wiki/Cat_show#Description_of_CFA_cat_shows_and_titles "Cat show") chocolate adult

The [breed standards](/wiki/Breed_standard "Breed standard") of various [cat fancier organisations](/wiki/Cat_registry "Cat registry") may treat the Himalayan and Exotic Shorthair (or simply Exotic) as variants of the Persian or as separate breeds.[[37]](#cite_note-WCC-37) The CFA treats the Himalayan as a colour-pattern class of both the Persian and the Exotic, which have separate but nearly identical standards (differing in coat length).[[40]](#cite_note-CFA_std-40) The [FIFe](/wiki/F%C3%A9d%C3%A9ration_Internationale_F%C3%A9line "Fédération Internationale Féline") entirely subsumes what other registries call the Himalayan as simply among the allowed colouration patterns for the Persian and the Exotic, treated as separate breeds.[[41]](#cite_note-FIFe_std-41) The International Cat Association (TICA) treats them both as variants of the Persian.[[23]](#cite_note-TICA_std-23) The [World Cat Federation](/wiki/World_Cat_Federation "World Cat Federation") (WCF) treats the Persian and Exotic Shorthair as separate breeds and subsumes the Himalayan colouration as colourpoint varieties under each.[[42]](#cite_note-WFC_std-42)

Among regional and national organisations, Feline Federation Europe treats all three as separate breeds.[[43]](#cite_note-FFE_std-43) The [American Cat Fanciers Association](/wiki/American_Cat_Fanciers_Association "American Cat Fanciers Association") (ACFA) has the three as separate breeds (also with a Non-pointed Himalayan that is similar to the Persian).[[44]](

Main article: [List of awards and nominations received by Ed Sheeran](/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Ed_Sheeran "List of awards and nominations received by Ed Sheeran")

On 19 October 2015, Sheeran received an honorary degree from the [University of Suffolk](/wiki/University_of_Suffolk "University of Suffolk") in Ipswich for his "outstanding contribution to music".[[296]](#cite_note-degree-297) Sheeran commented: "Suffolk is very much where I call home. Receiving this recognition is a real privilege".[[296]](#cite_note-degree-297) He was appointed [Member of the Order of the British Empire](/wiki/Member_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire "Member of the Order of the British Empire") (MBE) in the [2017 Birthday Honours](/wiki/2017_Birthday_Honours "2017 Birthday Honours") for "services to music and charity".[[297]](#cite_note-298) Sheeran received the award from [Prince Charles](/wiki/Prince_Charles "Prince Charles") at [Buckingham Palace](/wiki/Buckingham_Palace "Buckingham Palace") on 7 December 2017.[[298]](#cite_note-299) In 2012, he was named a [baron](/wiki/Baron "Baron") of [Sealand](/wiki/Sealand "Sealand").[[299]](#cite_note-300)

In addition to having the [highest-grossing concert tour](/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_concert_tours "List of highest-grossing concert tours") between 2017 and 2019, and being one of the [world's best-selling music artists](/wiki/World%27s_best-selling_music_artists "World's best-selling music artists") with 200 million records sold, Sheeran has received a number of awards.
